A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a dataset for denoising and benchmarking of images with varying noise levels and trained a model that outperforms BM-3D for unseen noise.
we introduce the first large-scale dataset of DSLR-like natural image noise and show that it can be used to train a denoising neural network that generalizes well to unseen images.
this dataset can be a great help to the researchers in the field of image denoising.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NIND dataset enables the training of denoisers with a much wider range of noise than was previously possible.
a dataset of real images with noise is necessary to train a model to denoise unseen images.
training with realistic noise distributions leads to better denoising performance than training with synthetic noise.
